evidence.quote: PATs are generated in the developer console.
You can generate a personal access token from the Asana developer console.
The Asana API is a RESTful interface with predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts JSON or form-encoded requests, returns JSON, and uses standard HTTP features.
Official Asana MCP server (V2) at https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp, requiring OAuth 2.0 authentication with a registered client ID and client secret

result.notes: Free self-serve access: any Asana user can generate a Personal Access Token from the developer console (app.asana.com/0/my-apps) with no paid plan or approval required, and PATs are passed as Bearer tokens. OAuth2 is the recommended method for multi-user apps and is also what the official MCP server (V2, launched Feb 2026) uses. A separate Service Account auth method exists but is Enterprise-tier/admin-only and is not counted here since PAT/OAuth already provide self-serve access. API is REST, ~167 endpoints per OpenAPI spec.
result.one_liner: Asana is a work-management and project-tracking platform with a REST API for tasks, projects, and portfolios.
